scope: Partial D06: recorded project authority across native API, pipeline/artifact selection, local MCP and typed approvals; no full security or release claim.

environment.host: macOS ARM64; disposable Linux Docker runners
environment.resources: Two CPUs per backend runner; native threads bounded at two. Provider keys blank, engine unavailable, telemetry disabled; optional SDK absent. Primary installation untouched.

checks.evidence: Explicit project activation; existing classification/regression, exact artifacts, batch scoring, keyboard approval/diagnostics and CSRF assertions retained; missing-artifact fixtures are now project-owned.

checks.name: Actual MCP stdio protocol
checks.evidence: Original actor/process scope/grant/direct-execution checks retained; project revocation and reviewer read/prepare checks added.

checks.name: Independent private PostgreSQL project processes
checks.evidence: Private verify-full TLS; two isolated projects, developer/reviewer/admin behavior, native and MCP revocation with an active MCP grant, unaffected reviewer and preserved browser sign-in.

checks.name: Private metadata restart and quiescent synthetic restore
checks.evidence: Existing authentication/TLS/CSRF checks retained; policy activation, membership revisions and dataset/pipeline project bindings persist across restart and matching database/artifact restore. Production recovery remains unqualified.

checks.name: Static/dependency/migration/frontend build checks
checks.evidence: Ruff; migration drift; pip consistency; changed Python script syntax; Angular build; ESLint has zero errors and 153 legacy warnings. Exact-head six-job CI remains a separate PR fact.

qualification_corrections: Governance checks mutate evidence and require developer authority; static purifier options remain a data-free catalog.
Successful authorized deletion recognizes the removed object while rechecking membership; it does not report a false denial.
Native encoding sidecars and immutable execution/assessment artifacts receive explicit owners; pathlib inputs are normalized only inside the trusted managed-path boundary.

PostgreSQL response-close tests use actual transaction lifecycles. Previously pure file-publication fixtures now provide metadata access because governed publication records artifact authority; all scientific assertions remain unchanged.

After the 1898-test full matrix, one additional authority recheck was added after evidence inspection. Its new regression and all 29 project cases pass on the final application source; all 29 governed browser/API cases repeat on that source. Final exact-head CI qualifies the complete updated tree separately.
ci: All six existing CI jobs remain. PostgreSQL additionally runs the five-process private project fixture; browser CI activates real project bindings and actual stdio tests add project roles/revocation. Exact-head CI is tracked by PR108 separately from local matrix source evidence.
limitations: Development installations without explicit activation retain legacy organization-wide authenticated behavior and are unqualified for project isolation. Governance activation has no supported downgrade.
Legacy adoption is a current operator assertion; it never invents historical ownership/provenance. Unregistered legacy media and incompatible frozen cross-project history exports are withheld.
Single-role membership, operator bootstrap/adoption and scoped admin API only. SSO/MFA/enrollment, project/reviewer UI and comprehensive accessibility remain open.
No recall of already delivered bytes and no cancellation/recovery of already authorized handlers/jobs. Interrupted access receipts may remain started.
Database and artifact administrators are trusted. Tamper-proof audit, retention/deletion, provider/embedding/telemetry/log egress and full threat-model qualification remain open.

No expert-isolation, independent reproduction, live private TLS ingress, offline/encrypted installation, production restore/upgrade, PostgreSQL dataset intake, customer capacity/value/acceptance or release claim.
